newsitem.title: USA: India seeks U.S. investors for projects.
newsitem.headline: India seeks U.S. investors for projects.

text.p: Indian officials visiting major U.S. cities said Friday they were seeking $250 billion in investment in construction projects.

The country needs $250 billion in the next 10 years to develop power plants, roads, ports, pipelines and telecommunications, said Cabinet Secretary T.S.R. Subramanian, who is leading a delegation of about 20 Indian government and business officials.

The visit was not designed to seal any deals, but to drum up interest in Indian projects, which used to be exclusively in the government's hands and were opened to the private sector last year, he said.

"This is basically to tell the investment community ... what we are doing, what are their concerns, what is it we can do further to make it easier for them to come, consistent with our own needs," Subramanian said at a news conference.
Based on interest expressed by American companies, he said he had no doubt the United States would remain India's largest trading partner and largest source of foreign investment.

"We expect that this trend will continue. From what we saw ... in New York and yesterday in Washington, we see no reason to change this," he said. The officials also plan to visit Los Angeles and San Francisco.
In talks with Commerce Department officials, the Indian officials voiced concern about U.S. export license restrictions on telecommunications and satellite technology.

In San Francisco, the delegation planned to focus on persuading U.S. companies and Indian entrepreneurs in Silicon Valley to use expertise in India. "We feel that the potential has not been scratched," Subramanian said.
